# ARCHITECTURE.md

A map of how this agent is put together, for humans and AI agents working in the repo. Keep it current as the codebase evolves.

## Project identification

- **Name:** eve Software Factory
- **Maintainer:** Vercel Labs (Ben Sabic)
- **License:** MIT
- **Last updated:** 2026-11-11

## Overview

This is a software factory built on the [eve](https://eve.dev) agent framework: the root agent is an orchestrator that takes work items from GitHub (an issue labeled `factory`, or an @Foreman mention), Linear (Agent Sessions), and an HTTP intake API (`POST /intake/v1/tickets`), and turns each into a draft pull request on `FACTORY_REPO`. Every item is triaged first by `triage_work_item`, a single decision-model call that classifies the item, picks labels from the repository's existing vocabulary, checks it against likely duplicates, and returns a lane: `pipeline`, `clarify`, `answer`, or `duplicate`. On the `pipeline` lane the item moves through the stations, each a declared subagent with its own instructions, sandbox, and tool surface: an optional **researcher** (web research for outside facts), the **analyst** (plan with acceptance criteria, grounded in a repo checkout), the **implementer** (executes the plan in its own checkout, runs the repo's checks, pushes a feature branch), and the **reviewer** (independent verdict on the pushed branch, different model vendor, up to 2 revision cycles). The **classifier** station is the fallback that writes clarifying questions on the `clarify` lane, or stands in when triage is unavailable. People stay in the loop where judgment lives: marking a PR ready stops the session to request approval, merging isn't in the tool surface at all, and unattended runs are denied everything except labels, progress comments on their own intake issue, closing or reopening issues, and draft PRs. Closing an issue runs ungated for every caller: it is reversible triage, and a reopen undoes it. The agent runs on Vercel, the same way locally (`eve dev`) and in production (`eve deploy`).

The factory works on GitHub with the real `gh` and `git` binaries, run inside sandboxes. What a command may do is decided by an argv allowlist, who may run it by one policy module, and what the credential can reach by a per-command lease on a narrowly scoped token. Memory (per-user preferences and the shared factory brain) is eve's built-in file memory, recalled before every turn.

eve discovers every capability from the filesystem under `agent/`. There is no central registry or wiring file: a tool's name is its filename, a subagent's name is its directory, a memory slot's name is its filename.

## Project structure

```text
agent/
  agent.ts                  # model configuration (defineAgent): compaction threshold + a session usage limit that asks before continuing
  instructions.ts           # defineInstructions: the orchestrator prompt, resolved at build time (injects FACTORY_REPO)
  channels/
    github.ts               # eve GitHub channel via Vercel Connect; botName resolved from the connector's app slug; wires the four hooks from lib/github/hooks.ts
    linear.ts               # eve Linear channel via Connect; Agent Sessions; stamps trusted (workspace membership is the gate), injects requester name
    intake.ts               # custom channel: POST /intake/v1/tickets and GET /intake/v1/tickets/:ticketId; unattended runs, optional signed callbacks
    eve.ts                  # inbound route auth; dev-only localDevUser shim (user principal, allowAgentInfo, allowToolStubs)
  connections/
    linear.ts               # Linear MCP server (mcp.linear.app); app-scoped auth via linearAuth; writes denied on unattended runs
  memory/
    preferences.ts          # slot "preferences": file memory, one document per signed-in user (userScope)
    brain.ts                # slot "brain": the factory brain, writable (trust-gated) on the orchestrator
  sandbox.ts                # root sandbox (Vercel Sandbox); the GitHub channel checks the triggering thread's ref out here, and the orchestrator's gh runs here
  subagents/
    classifier/             # agent.ts (tool: false) + instructions.md; text-only; writes clarifying questions, fallback when triage fails
    researcher/             # agent.ts (tool: false) + instructions.md + tools/save_artifact.ts; fresh-context web researcher
    analyst/                # agent.ts (tool: false) + instructions.md + sandbox.ts (repo clone) + memory/brain.ts (read-only) + tools/{gh,git,glob,grep,save_artifact,read_artifact}.ts; plans, never writes
    implementer/            # agent.ts (tool: false) + instructions.md + sandbox.ts + memory/brain.ts (read-only) + tools/{gh,git,glob,grep,read_artifact}.ts; the one station whose git may push
    reviewer/               # agent.ts (different vendor, tool: false) + instructions.md + sandbox.ts + memory/brain.ts (read-only) + tools/{gh,git,glob,grep,read_artifact}.ts
  tools/
    agent.ts                # disableTool(): the built-in agent tool would let the root bypass its stations
    bash.ts, write_file.ts, edit_file.ts
                             # disableTool(): the orchestrator has no shell and cannot write files, so gh is the only process it can start
    gh.ts                   # the orchestrator's gh: ghTool({ mode: "full" }), writes gated by ghPolicy
    triage_work_item.ts     # decision-model triage: classify, pick labels, check duplicates, return a lane; applies labels under the label policy
    diagnose_ci_failure.ts  # reads a PR's failing checks and logs, classifies the cause with the decision model; read-only
    run_classifier.ts, run_researcher.ts, run_analyst.ts, run_implementer.ts, run_reviewer.ts
                             # defineWorkflowTool wrappers: the model-facing entry point for each station. Each blocks on
                             # ctx.agent(id).send(message, { outputSchema, signal }).result() and passes the result through
                             # stationOutput(), attaching the matching schema from lib/stations/schemas.ts.
    read_artifact.ts        # Blob: read a handoff artifact by id (read-only, open to every run)
    glob.ts, grep.ts        # re-exports of eve's built-in glob and grep
  lib/
    constants.ts            # requireEnv + FACTORY_REPO/factoryRepo/FACTORY_LABEL/FACTORY_BRANCH_PREFIX + linearAuth
    models.ts               # the MODELS map: one model id per agent, plus the decision model
    trust.ts                # the single trust authority: AUTONOMOUS_PRINCIPAL, stampTrusted, stampAutonomous, autonomousForTicket, isAutonomous, isTrusted, isScheduleAppAuth, intakeIssueNumber
    blob.ts                 # the shared Blob layer: reserved-namespace registry (all prefixes + guards) and read/write/delete document helpers
    artifacts/              # handoff artifacts: config.ts (id pattern, kinds) + tools.ts (save/read tool factories)
    stations/
      schemas.ts            # the five stations' JSON output schemas, shared by each station's run_<id>.ts wrapper
      result.ts             # stationOutput(): throws for a failed, cancelled, or empty station result
    memory/
      brain.ts              # factoryBrain({ writable }): FACTORY_REPO scope, shared namespace, trustedWrites / readOnly provider wrappers
      scope.ts              # userScope: a scope for signed-in users only, null for everyone else
    triage/
      decisions.ts          # the decision-model question sets and thresholds: triageWorkItem, laneFor, diagnoseCiFailure
      github.ts             # the gh reads and writes triage needs: fetchIssue, fetchLabels, findDuplicateCandidates, applyLabels, fetchChecks, fetchFailedLogs
    intake/
      ticket.ts             # the ticket schema, ticket id derivation, callback allowlist, HMAC signature helpers
    github/
      credentials.ts        # GITHUB_CONNECTOR + the shared Connect credentials handle for the channel and the session clone
      cli.ts                # parseGh: the gh argv allowlist (COMMANDS) and the effect each invocation reduces to
      git-cli.ts            # parseGitNetwork: fetch / pull / ls-remote / push against the literal repository URL
      approval.ts           # the one policy module: ghPolicy, readOnlyGhPolicy, ghEffectDecision, the per-effect decisions, factoryBrainPolicy
      lease.ts              # credential leases: scoped token minting (TOKEN_SCOPES), firewall placeholder swap, runGh, runGitNetwork
      tools.ts              # ghTool and gitTool factories mounted by the orchestrator and the stations
      tooling.ts            # installFactoryTooling (gh + pnpm in sandbox prepare) and FACTORY_TOOLING_VERSION
      hooks.ts              # the GitHub channel's dispatch hooks and injected tasks: onComment, onIssue, onCheckSuite, onPullRequest
      git-remote.ts         # validateRef, validateBranch, REMOTE_URL, REPO_DIR, brokerPolicy and mintInstallationToken for the session clone
      repo-sandbox.ts       # FACTORY_SANDBOX_CREATE_OPTIONS, createFactoryEnvironment, factoryInit (clone + setup command per session)
      bot-name.ts           # resolves the @mention name from FACTORY_BOT_NAME or the connector's app slug
      bootstrap-diagnostics.ts # turns clone and token failures into messages that name FACTORY_REPO and the fix
  skills/                   # load-on-demand procedures, routed by description frontmatter
    writing-quality/        # AI-tells, plain English, prose specs
    triaging-issues/        # grounding a GitHub work item: dedupe, repo-native labels, ask-or-proceed, repro requests
    github-linear-bridging/ # bridged Linear issues: dedupe check, backlinks, team choice, two-way links
evals/                      # eve eval runner suite: smoke, routing/, safety/, pipeline/ (opt-in real run), helpers.ts, evals.config.ts
tests/                      # vitest suite, deterministic and offline: github/, intake/, memory/, triage/, surface/, helpers.ts
scripts/                    # discovery.ts (runs eve info --json and parses the report) + check-discovery.ts (pnpm run discovery)
vitest.config.ts            # test configuration: placeholder env for modules that validate it at load
```

## Core components

| Component | Lives in | eve primitive | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Orchestrator | `agent/agent.ts` + `instructions.ts` | Agent | Triages each work item, routes it through the stations in order, verifies handoffs, runs the review loop (max 2 cycles), opens the draft PR, reports back; never writes code itself and has no shell |
| GitHub surface | `agent/channels/github.ts` + `agent/lib/github/hooks.ts` | Channel | Intake and delivery: association-gated @Foreman mentions (stamped trusted), `factory`-label intake (rewritten to the autonomous principal, unattended framing injected), red-CI fix runs on `factory/*` PRs, PR summary comments on opened PRs; replies render in-thread |
| Linear surface | `agent/channels/linear.ts` | Channel | Linear Agent Sessions: users delegate issues to the factory; every session is stamped trusted (workspace membership); elicitations render natively |
| Intake API | `agent/channels/intake.ts` + `agent/lib/intake/ticket.ts` | Channel (custom) | Tickets in over HTTP: authenticates the caller, validates a strict schema, starts an unattended session under the autonomous principal, reports status and the final message, optionally POSTs signed callbacks |
| Route auth | `agent/channels/eve.ts` | Channel | Inbound auth for the eve route; the `localDevUser` shim upgrades the dev principal to a user so user-scoped memory works in the dev TUI, and keeps `/eve/v1/info` and tool stubs available to local `eve eval` |
| `gh` and `git` tools | `agent/lib/github/tools.ts`, mounted at `agent/tools/gh.ts` and each repo station's `tools/{gh,git}.ts` | Tools | The GitHub surface: the real binaries run in the mounting agent's sandbox with `{ args: string[] }` input. Full `gh` on the orchestrator, read-only `gh` on stations, networked `git` on stations (push on the implementer only) |
| Argv allowlists | `agent/lib/github/cli.ts`, `agent/lib/github/git-cli.ts` | Library | Parse every invocation against a fixed table of commands and flags, pin it to `FACTORY_REPO`, and reduce a `gh` invocation to one effect; anything unlisted is refused with a reason |
| Authorization policy | `agent/lib/github/approval.ts` | Library | The one place an effect and a caller class become run, wait for approval, or denied; also holds the brain's write policy |
| Credential leases | `agent/lib/github/lease.ts` | Library | Mints a repository- and permission-scoped installation token per command, hands the process a placeholder, and has the sandbox firewall swap it in; resets the policy afterwards |
| Decision-model triage | `agent/tools/triage_work_item.ts`, `agent/tools/diagnose_ci_failure.ts` + `agent/lib/triage/` | Tools | Fast, closed-question judgments through eve's `decide`: classification, label selection, duplicate check, lane; and the cause of a red CI run |
| Trust authority | `agent/lib/trust.ts` | Library | The only place caller trust is defined: trusted (stamped at dispatch), autonomous (label intake, CI fixes, intake tickets), schedule app auth; new capabilities gate on these predicates rather than inventing their own checks |
| classifier | `agent/subagents/classifier/` + `agent/tools/run_classifier.ts` | Subagent | Language-model classification that also writes the clarifying questions; called on the `clarify` lane or when triage fails |
| researcher | `agent/subagents/researcher/` + `agent/tools/run_researcher.ts` | Subagent | Fresh-context web research for facts the repo and tracker don't hold, called through its workflow-tool wrapper; returns cited findings + gaps |
| analyst | `agent/subagents/analyst/` + `agent/tools/run_analyst.ts` | Subagent | Planning against its own repo checkout, called through its workflow-tool wrapper; returns problem statement, approach, plan, risks, acceptance criteria, test strategy |
| implementer | `agent/subagents/implementer/` + `agent/tools/run_implementer.ts` | Subagent | Implementation in its own checkout, called through its workflow-tool wrapper: branch, code, run the repo's checks, commit, push with the `git` tool; returns branch + change summary + verification |
| reviewer | `agent/subagents/reviewer/` + `agent/tools/run_reviewer.ts` | Subagent | Independent review on a different vendor, called through its workflow-tool wrapper: fetch the branch with the `git` tool, read the real diff, judge each acceptance criterion; returns approve/request_changes/reject |
| Linear access | `agent/connections/linear.ts` | Connection (MCP) | Create issues, comment, cross-reference; app-scoped auth via `linearAuth`; denied on unattended runs |
| User preferences | `agent/memory/preferences.ts` + `agent/lib/memory/scope.ts` | Memory slot | Per-user standing preferences in eve file memory, scoped to the resolved `user` principal (never model input); off for every other caller. Tools: `preferences__save_memory`, `preferences__remove_memory` |
| Factory brain | `agent/memory/brain.ts`, `agent/subagents/{analyst,implementer,reviewer}/memory/brain.ts` + `agent/lib/memory/brain.ts` | Memory slot | Shared, durable notes about the target repository, scoped to `FACTORY_REPO`; recalled by the orchestrator and the three repo stations, written only on the orchestrator through `brain__save_memory` / `brain__remove_memory` under `factoryBrainPolicy` |
| Handoff artifacts | `agent/lib/artifacts/` + per-station `tools/{save,read}_artifact.ts` + root `agent/tools/read_artifact.ts` | Tools | Long Markdown documents stations pass by id in Blob: researcher and analyst save, analyst/implementer/reviewer read, the orchestrator relays only the id; ids validated by an anchored pattern so they can't escape the reserved prefix |
| Sandbox tooling | `agent/lib/github/tooling.ts` + `agent/lib/github/repo-sandbox.ts` | Sandbox | Installs `gh` and pnpm once per template snapshot (`prepare`); clones `FACTORY_REPO` and runs `FACTORY_SETUP_COMMAND` once per station session (`factoryInit`) |
| Skills | `agent/skills/` | Skill | Load-on-demand procedures: `writing-quality`, `triaging-issues`, `github-linear-bridging` |
| Tests | `tests/` | Vitest | Deterministic, offline checks of the allowlists, the authorization matrix, leases, hooks, memory, triage, the intake API, and the assembled surface |
| Evals | `evals/` | Evals | eve eval runner: routing and safety assertions against a real model (deny-by-default: every `gh` call must parse as an allowlisted read), an opt-in full-pipeline run |

Channels and the connection are I/O boundaries. Tools run in the app runtime (full `process.env`); the `gh` and `git` tools run their commands inside the mounting agent's sandbox. Skills only add instructions to context. Every station sets `tool: false` and is called through its `run_<id>` workflow tool, which blocks on `ctx.agent(id).send(message, { outputSchema, signal }).result()`, so the orchestrator still gets structured output back from a single call; a failed or cancelled station surfaces as a tool error through `stationOutput()`. Nothing in a station's own tool surface may need approval, since nobody is watching that station's card (see Security considerations).

## Data flow

1. **Unattended intake (`factory` label):** a maintainer labels an issue `factory`. The `issues` webhook hits `onIssue`, which dispatches only on the `labeled` action and only after verifying the labeler holds at least triage permission on the repository (GitHub fires `labeled` even for labels attached at creation, which issue templates let unauthenticated reporters do). The session's auth is rewritten to the constructed autonomous principal, and an injected task frames the run: never ask, post questions and stop if clarification is needed, deliver a draft PR. The pipeline runs; the orchestrator opens the draft PR (`gh pr create --draft` needs no approval) and announces it in the closing reply the channel delivers to the issue.
2. **Unattended intake (HTTP ticket):** a caller POSTs a ticket to `/intake/v1/tickets`. The channel authenticates the caller (a Vercel OIDC token for the project, the `FACTORY_INTAKE_TOKEN` bearer, or `localDev()` in `eve dev`), validates the body against a strict schema, derives a ticket id, and starts a session at the address `ticket:<ticketId>` under the autonomous principal built by `autonomousForTicket`. It answers `202` with `ticketId`, `sessionId`, and `deliveryId`; resubmitting the same `externalId` from the same caller answers `200` with `duplicate: true` and the original session. There is no issue thread, so the run posts no comments: its final message (the draft PR link, or the clarifying questions) is the result, read with `GET /intake/v1/tickets/:ticketId`, which reports `queued`, `running`, `awaiting-input`, `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`. With an allowlisted `callbackUrl` and a configured secret, the channel also POSTs signed updates when a turn settles, an interaction opens, or the session fails.
3. **Red CI on a factory PR:** a `check_suite` webhook with a failure conclusion, anchored to a pull request whose head branch starts with `factory/`, hits `onCheckSuite`. The session runs unattended on that PR's thread. The injected task self-limits: count earlier fix-attempt comments on the PR (each fresh session's only shared memory is the thread), stop and hand off to a person after 2. Otherwise it calls `diagnose_ci_failure`, which reads the failing checks and failed-step logs with `gh` and asks the decision model for the cause. Only when `fix_with_code` is true does the run post an attempt comment and send an implementer/reviewer revision that pushes to the same branch; a flaky, infrastructure, or configuration failure gets one explanatory comment and no fix attempt. Suites on branches people pushed never dispatch.
4. **Attended intake (@Foreman mention):** `onComment` keeps the built-in mention and ignore rules, dispatches only for OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR commenters, and stamps `attributes.trusted`. The pipeline runs with the requester on the other end: clarifying questions go to them, reversible writes run without cards, shipping actions stop and wait for approval.
5. **Linear sessions:** a user delegates an issue in Linear; `onAgentSession` stamps trusted and injects the requester's name. The factory works the item, posts progress as Agent Activities, and reports the PR link back on the session. Cross-tracker conventions come from the `github-linear-bridging` skill.
6. **The pipeline itself:** the orchestrator reads the real work item, then calls `triage_work_item` (with `issue_number` for a GitHub issue, or the title and body verbatim otherwise). The tool reads the issue, the repository's labels, and duplicate candidates with `gh`, asks one decision-model call for the classification, a yes/no per existing label, and a yes/no per candidate, applies the selected labels, and returns the lane. `clarify` goes to the classifier for the questions to ask, `answer` is answered without building, `duplicate` is checked by the orchestrator before it acts, and `pipeline` delegates in order: optional researcher (when `needs_research` is true) → analyst (reads its checkout) → implementer (branches, implements, verifies, pushes with its `git` tool) → reviewer (fetches the branch, judges the real diff). `request_changes` loops back to the implementer at most twice. Every delegation message is self-contained; stations never see the orchestrator's history, though the analyst, implementer, and reviewer recall the factory brain themselves. Long documents skip the inline path: the researcher and analyst can save a handoff artifact and return its id in `artifact_id`, the orchestrator relays the id, and downstream stations read the document themselves with `read_artifact`.
7. **A GitHub command, end to end:** the model calls `gh` with an argv array. The tool's approval function parses the argv with `parseGh`; a refused argv is denied with the reason, and an accepted one is reduced to an effect that `ghEffectDecision` maps to run, wait, or denied for the caller's class. On run, `runGh` mints a token for the scope (`repo-read` for reads, `repo-triage` for writes), writes any `--body` text to a temp file and passes `--body-file`, sets a firewall policy that swaps a random placeholder for the token on `api.github.com` and `uploads.github.com`, runs `/usr/bin/gh` with `GH_TOKEN` set to the placeholder and `GH_REPO` set to `FACTORY_REPO`, and resets the policy in a `finally`. Output is redacted and truncated before the model sees it. A station's `git` tool follows the same path through `parseGitNetwork` and `runGitNetwork`, with the placeholder carried in git's own config through the environment and swapped on `github.com` and `codeload.github.com`.
8. **PR opened (by someone else):** `onPullRequest` dispatches on the `opened` action (bot senders skipped, which covers `foreman[bot]`'s own PRs) with a summary task injected; the agent posts one orienting comment with a changed-files table.
9. **Learning:** when a run surfaces a durable fact about the repository, the orchestrator saves it to the brain with `brain__save_memory`. An unattended run has no brain tools, so it puts the fact in its final reply as a suggested note for a maintainer to record.

## Data stores

- **GitHub** (external): the repository and issue tracker the factory works on. Access goes through the `gh` and `git` binaries in sandboxes, authenticated at the sandbox firewall with installation tokens minted through Vercel Connect (see Security).
- **Linear** (external): where delegated work arrives and cross-references land. Access via Linear's MCP server with app-scoped Connect auth (scopes `read`, `write`, `issues:create`, `comments:create`).
- **eve file memory**: the `preferences` documents (one per signed-in user) and the `brain` document (one per `FACTORY_REPO`). Deployed, eve stores them in a private Vercel Blob store connected under the `EVE_MEMORY_BLOB` prefix (`eve integration setup file-memory` provisions it and sets `EVE_MEMORY_BLOB_STORE_ID`); when that is absent eve falls back to the application's own Blob configuration (`BLOB_STORE_ID` or `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`). In `eve dev` the documents live in process-local memory and are gone when the process exits. eve recalls each document before every turn; one entry is at most 2,048 bytes and a stored document at most 65,536 bytes, and the brain's recalled message is capped at 8,000 characters.
- **Vercel Blob** (the application's store): handoff artifacts under the reserved `artifacts/<validated-id>.md` prefix, reachable only through the artifact tools. Authenticated by the project's OIDC token. `agent/lib/blob.ts` also reserves `eve/memory/` and the legacy `user-preferences/` and `factory-brain/` prefixes that earlier versions wrote memory under; nothing reads those legacy documents anymore and they are not migrated.
- **Session and channel state** (eve): the intake channel keeps `ticketId` and `callbackUrl` as per-session channel state, and a ticket's status is derived from its session's recorded events. There is no ticket table.
- **Vercel Sandbox**: the root sandbox holds the GitHub channel's thread checkout and is where the orchestrator's `gh` runs; each repo-facing station's sandbox holds its own clone of `FACTORY_REPO`, cloned fresh per session by `factoryInit`. Template snapshots carry the installed tooling (`gh`, pnpm), not the repository. Not durable application stores.

There is no application database. Anything that must outlive a session (for example, cross-run sweep state for a future schedule) belongs in an external store.

## External integrations

| Integration | Purpose | Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub | Label intake, mentions, CI and PR events in; comments, labels, branches, and draft PRs out | eve GitHub channel via Vercel Connect (`GITHUB_CONNECTOR`); the `gh` and `git` binaries in sandboxes, with per-command installation tokens from `@vercel/connect` `getToken` swapped in at the sandbox firewall |
| Linear (channel + MCP) | Agent Sessions in; issue creation, comments, cross-references out | eve Linear channel via Connect; MCP connection to `mcp.linear.app` with app-scoped auth shared through `linearAuth` (`LINEAR_CONNECTOR`) |
| Intake API callers | Tickets in over HTTP, status out, optional callbacks out | Custom channel routes `POST /intake/v1/tickets` and `GET /intake/v1/tickets/:ticketId`; bearer secret or Vercel OIDC; callbacks signed with HMAC-SHA256 |
| Vercel Blob | eve file memory (preferences, factory brain) and station handoff artifacts | eve's file-memory backend for memory; `@vercel/blob` for artifacts; OIDC-authenticated |
| Vercel AI Gateway | Model access for the root, every station, and the decision model | Gateway model ids, all in `agent/lib/models.ts` (the reviewer deliberately runs a different vendor than the implementer; `decision` is `typesafe-ai/jev`) |
| Vercel Sandbox | Isolated runtimes: root checkout + three station clones | `agent/sandbox.ts` and `agent/subagents/*/sandbox.ts` (`VercelSandbox.environment()`, shared options and builders in `agent/lib/github/repo-sandbox.ts`) |

## Deployment & infrastructure

- **Platform:** Vercel, Node 24. Deploy with `eve deploy` (wraps `vercel deploy --prod`; the raw command cannot auto-detect the eve framework).
- **Connectors:** provisioned via `vercel connect create` + `attach`; the GitHub trigger points at `/eve/v1/github` (subscribe to `issues`, `issue_comment`, `pull_request_review_comment`, `pull_request`, and `check_suite`) and the Linear trigger at `/eve/v1/linear` (AgentSessionEvent).
- **GitHub App permissions:** the installation needs write access to contents, issues, and pull requests on `FACTORY_REPO`. CI diagnosis (`gh pr checks`, `gh run view --log-failed`) also needs Actions read and Checks read; commit statuses read is requested when granted. Workflows write is optional and only matters when a change touches `.github/workflows`. The factory asks for less than the app holds on each command (see token scopes under Security), so granting a permission does not hand it to every command.
- **Memory storage:** run `eve integration setup file-memory` in the linked project, then redeploy. It creates or reuses a private Blob store, connects it with the `EVE_MEMORY_BLOB` prefix, and sets `EVE_MEMORY_BLOB_STORE_ID`; there is nothing to fill in by hand.
- **Intake routes:** `POST /intake/v1/tickets` and `GET /intake/v1/tickets/:ticketId` are served by the same deployment. Set `FACTORY_INTAKE_TOKEN` (at least 32 characters) to let callers outside Vercel submit; leave it unset and only callers holding a Vercel OIDC token for the project can.
- **Environment:** connector UIDs `GITHUB_CONNECTOR` and `LINEAR_CONNECTOR`; `FACTORY_REPO` (required at module load; a missing value fails discovery). Optional: `FACTORY_SETUP_COMMAND` (runs inside the clone once per station session), `FACTORY_LABEL`, `FACTORY_BRANCH_PREFIX`, `FACTORY_BOT_NAME`, `FACTORY_INTAKE_TOKEN`, `FACTORY_INTAKE_CALLBACK_HOSTS` (comma-separated hosts callbacks may go to), `FACTORY_INTAKE_CALLBACK_SECRET` (signs callbacks; none are sent without it), and `FACTORY_STRICT_TOKEN_SCOPES` (`1` refuses the fallback to the app's full permissions). The model and Blob authenticate via the project's OIDC token.
- **Local development:** `pnpm dev` runs the same runtime in a TUI; `vercel env pull` supplies a short-lived OIDC token (needed for Connect and the sandboxes). The webhook surfaces run against a deployment; point the TUI at one with `eve remote connect --url <url>`. The dev principal is untrusted by design, so approval cards surface in the TUI. Memory is process-local in `eve dev`.

## Security considerations

- **Trust is decided at dispatch, not in the prompt.** The channel hooks decide who the caller is on the signed webhook (or the authenticated intake request) and stamp it into session auth (`attributes.trusted`, or the constructed autonomous principal). `agent/lib/trust.ts` is the single authority reading those stamps; a new capability never invents its own caller check.
- **Three caller classes, one policy module.** `agent/lib/github/approval.ts` returns `not-applicable` (run), `user-approval` (stop and wait for a person), or `denied`. Unattended runs (label intake, CI fixes, intake tickets) are denied rather than left waiting: nobody is watching to answer, and a server-side denial costs one step instead of a stranded session. Trusted callers (a stamped mention, a Linear session, a schedule turn) run routine reversible writes without a prompt. Everyone else (the dev TUI, an unstamped session) waits for a person on writes.
- **The argv allowlist is the tool surface.** The model writes ordinary `gh` commands, and `parseGh` accepts only the commands and flags listed in `COMMANDS`; an unlisted command or flag is refused with a reason before anything reaches a sandbox, so a new `gh` feature is unreachable until someone decides what it is. Short-flag clusters, glued values, and `--` are refused rather than guessed at. `--repo` must name `FACTORY_REPO` and is stripped; `GH_REPO` pins the repository. There is no `pr merge`, no `pr review`, no repository, secret, auth, or release-writing command, and no `--web` or `--editor`.
- **`gh api` is GET-only.** It accepts no method other than GET, no field flags (which would turn a call into a POST), only `Accept` and `X-GitHub-Api-Version` headers, and only plain paths under `repos/<FACTORY_REPO>/`. Changing something always goes through a named subcommand whose effect the policy knows.
- **Effects decide the outcome.** Each accepted invocation reduces to `read`, `label`, `comment`, `state`, `draft-pr`, `write`, or `ship`. Reads, closing or reopening an issue, and opening a draft PR run for every caller. Labels run for unattended and trusted callers. A comment from an unattended run is allowed only on the thread it was dispatched from, and a close or reopen that attaches a comment is held to the same comment rule. A draft that requests reviewers or assignees is a `write`, since it notifies people.
- **Draft PRs are the unattended ceiling.** Anything that can ship (`pr ready`, a non-draft `pr create`) waits for a person even when the caller is trusted, and is denied unattended. Merge is not in the allowlist at all, and the token the orchestrator's writes run on could not merge anyway (below).
- **The orchestrator has no shell.** Its `bash`, `write_file`, and `edit_file` tools are disabled, as is the built-in `agent` tool. With no way to run a command or write a file, the only process the orchestrator can start in its sandbox is `gh` with an argv the allowlist accepted. That is what makes the allowlist a boundary rather than a suggestion: the session that reads untrusted issue text and holds the write-capable policy cannot run anything else next to a live credential. It can still read the checkout (`read_file`, `glob`, `grep`).
- **Credentials are leased per command and never enter a sandbox.** For each `gh` or networked `git` command, `lease.ts` mints an installation token in the app runtime, gives the process a random placeholder (`GH_TOKEN` for `gh`; an `http.extraheader` passed through `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment variables for git), and sets a sandbox firewall policy that replaces the `authorization` header with the real token only on requests that carry that exact placeholder, and only to `api.github.com` and `uploads.github.com` (gh) or `github.com` and `codeload.github.com` (git). The policy goes back to `allow-all` in a `finally`, leases are serialized per sandbox so two commands can't clear each other's policy, and the token is redacted from output. A leased git command runs with hooks disabled and HTTPS as its only allowed protocol.
- **Tokens are scoped to the repository and the command class.** Each lease requests a token for `FACTORY_REPO` alone with one of three permission sets: `repo-read` (contents, issues, and pull requests read; station `gh` and `git` fetches), `repo-triage` (issues and pull requests write, contents read; the orchestrator's `gh` writes, which therefore cannot merge or push), and `repo-push` (contents write; the implementer's `git push` only). CI read permissions and workflows write are requested as optional extras. If the installation refuses a narrowed set, minting retries with the required permissions alone, and then falls back to the app's full permissions on the factory repository with a console warning, because a factory that stops working over a hardening step is the worse failure. Set `FACTORY_STRICT_TOKEN_SCOPES=1` to make that last fallback an error instead.
- **Git can only reach the factory repository, and only feature branches.** `parseGitNetwork` accepts `fetch`, `pull`, `ls-remote`, and `push`. The remote is never taken from the caller: the word `origin` is replaced with the literal `https://github.com/<FACTORY_REPO>.git`, because remote config in a sandbox is model-writable. Refs must be plain branch names (no refspecs, no `refs/` prefix, no `HEAD`); `push` refuses `main` and `master`, and force, delete, mirror, and tag pushes are not in the allowlist. Only the implementer's tool accepts `push`.
- **Stations hold no approvable tools.** A declared subagent can technically request input, but nothing is watching a station's own approval card, so nothing inside a station may need one; that is a design convention this codebase follows, not a framework guarantee. A station's `gh` runs reads and denies everything else (`readOnlyGhPolicy`), and its `git` either runs or is denied. The orchestrator owns every write to GitHub except the implementer's branch push, and a feature branch alone ships nothing.
- **Label intake can't be forged by reporters.** GitHub fires the `labeled` action even for labels attached at issue creation, which issue templates let unauthenticated reporters do, so the hook verifies the labeler's repository permission against the API before dispatching; anyone below triage is acknowledged without a session, and a failed lookup fails closed.
- **Mention authorization:** `onComment` dispatches only for OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR commenters; everyone else's mentions never start a session. The PR-opened hook deliberately isn't association-gated (summarizing outside PRs is the feature) but its task is scoped to one summary comment, and the dispatched session carries no trusted stamp, so its writes wait for approval.
- **Approval prompts on GitHub:** the channel posts pending input requests as comments by default, with a mention-based reply instruction. The channel's `botName` is fed the connector-resolved name, which keeps that instruction and the reply's mention-stripping correct. Answers route back through the same `onComment` mention gate, which is what makes a comment reply an authorization signal rather than a race anyone on a public repo can win: an untrusted account's "approve" never reaches the waiting session.
- **Intake API authentication.** A request must carry a Vercel OIDC token minted for the project or the `FACTORY_INTAKE_TOKEN` bearer (`localDev()` is accepted only on a development server). The shared secret is compared in constant time after hashing both sides, never matches when unset or shorter than 32 characters, and a bearer that is present but wrong is rejected outright instead of falling through to the next authenticator. The token is read from the `Authorization` header only.
- **Intake tickets cannot choose who they run as.** The schema is strict (an unknown field is a 400, the body is capped at 64 KiB), and the session's principal is built from the verified caller and a server-made ticket id alone. The ticket's requester, priority, and labels are rendered into the first message as the submitter's unverified claims. The run is unattended, so it is held to what every unattended run may do, and since no issue number is stamped it has no thread to comment on: it can read, apply labels, close or reopen an issue, and open a draft PR.
- **Intake idempotency and isolation.** With an `externalId`, the ticket id is a digest of the verified caller and that id, so a retry lands on the session the first submission started, two callers can't collide or guess each other's ids, and the delivery carries a matching idempotency key for two submissions racing each other. Status reads resolve the session through the ticket's own address, never a raw session id, so the API cannot be used to read a session GitHub or Linear started.
- **Intake callbacks are allowlisted and signed.** A caller-supplied URL the server will POST to is a request-forgery vector, so a `callbackUrl` must be HTTPS, carry no credentials, and name a host listed exactly in `FACTORY_INTAKE_CALLBACK_HOSTS`; otherwise the ticket is refused with `callback_not_allowed`. Callbacks are sent only when `FACTORY_INTAKE_CALLBACK_SECRET` is set, carry `x-factory-signature` (hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body) and an `idempotency-key`, do not follow redirects, time out after 10 seconds, and never fail the run: `GET /intake/v1/tickets/:ticketId` stays the source of truth.
- **Prompt-injection surface:** the factory reads third-party issue bodies, comments, diffs, and intake tickets, and its stations execute repository code (tests, lint) inside sandboxes. The bounds are structural: unattended sessions run under the denied-by-default autonomous principal, triage is a decision model that can only pick among given options (the worst a hostile issue body earns is a wrong label), the Linear connection denies unattended writes, the orchestrator has no shell, credentials are leased and scoped, and everything that ships needs a human. Instruction-following on injected text remains model judgment; the evals' prompt-injection case keeps a floor under it.
- **Inbound route auth** (`agent/channels/eve.ts`): `[localDevUser, vercelOidc()]` rejects public browser traffic; channel traffic is authenticated by each connector, and the intake routes by their own authenticators.
- **Per-user isolation:** the `preferences` slot's scope comes from the resolved principal, never from model input, and only a `user` principal has one. The constructed service principals unattended runs execute under resolve to `null`, so a prompt-injected issue can't leave "preferences" behind for the next unattended run to obey.
- **Memory write gating:** recalled memory is context every future run trusts. The brain's scope is `FACTORY_REPO`, never model input, so a session can't redirect a read or write to another document. Unattended runs get no brain tools at all (`trustedWrites`), and `factoryBrainPolicy` is the second lock: it denies the autonomous principal, lets trusted callers write directly, and makes everyone else wait on an approval card. Station mounts are recall-only. Recalled entries are framed to the model as facts someone wrote down, not instructions.
- **Artifact-id containment:** artifact ids are the one Blob address the model supplies, so `artifactKey` accepts only ids matching the anchored `ARTIFACT_ID_PATTERN` (lowercase alphanumerics and hyphens, no dots or slashes) before interpolating them into a key under the reserved `artifacts/` prefix; an invalid id reads as `found: false`, indistinguishable from a missing one. Saves never overwrite (`allowOverwrite: false`), are size-bounded, and mint their own suffixed id, which is what lets both artifact tools live ungated inside a station.

### Residual risks

These are known and not closed by this design. Read them before pointing the factory at a repository that matters.

- **A station runs repository code and holds a shell.** The analyst, implementer, and reviewer execute the target repository's own scripts in a sandbox that also has `bash`. During a push lease, anything in the implementer's sandbox that learns the placeholder (it is in the leased process's environment) could use it to push to any branch the `repo-push` token allows, not only the branch the tool named. The branch checks live in the argv parser, not in the token. Protect the default branch on GitHub (branch protection or a ruleset that requires pull requests) so the token's reach stops there.
- **The session clone and the setup command run under a broader credential window.** `factoryInit` clones `FACTORY_REPO` and then runs `FACTORY_SETUP_COMMAND` while a firewall policy attaches the connector's installation token to every request to `github.com` from that sandbox, with no placeholder match and no permission narrowing. A setup command such as `pnpm install` runs the repository's install scripts inside that window. This predates the lease model and was not moved onto it in this change.
- **The GitHub channel's own checkout leaves a credentialed policy on the root sandbox.** eve's per-turn checkout sets a network policy that injects the installation token on git requests to GitHub and does not reset it; the policy stays until the orchestrator's next `gh` call ends its lease and sets `allow-all`. This matters less than it used to, because the root has no shell and no file-writing tool, but it is a window the factory does not control.
- **Token permission narrowing has not been exercised against a live installation.** The scopes are requested through Vercel Connect's `authorizationDetails`, and the fallback path exists because installations differ. Whether a given installation honours the narrowed sets is only known once it runs; watch the logs for the fallback warning, and set `FACTORY_STRICT_TOKEN_SCOPES=1` once the narrowed sets are confirmed to work.
- **`gh` is installed unpinned.** `installFactoryTooling` takes `gh` from the sandbox image's Ubuntu archive (signed and verified by apt) at whatever version the archive carries when a template snapshot is built. A flag the allowlist names could behave differently across versions. pnpm is likewise installed at the current npm version.
- **Model judgment is still in the loop.** The allowlist and the policy bound what an action can do, not whether it was the right action: a wrong label, a misleading comment on the intake thread, or a poor draft PR are all within an unattended run's permissions.

## Development & testing

- **Runtime/TUI:** `pnpm dev` (eve dev TUI; `/login` links a model provider, `/model` switches models).
- **Type checking:** `pnpm typecheck` (tsc; covers `agent/`, `evals/`, `tests/`, and `scripts/`).
- **Lint/format:** `pnpm check` / `pnpm fix` (Ultracite, a Biome preset; config in `biome.jsonc`).
- **Tests:** `pnpm test` (vitest; `pnpm test:watch` to watch). The suite is deterministic and offline: it never reaches a model, GitHub, Linear, Blob, or a sandbox, and `vitest.config.ts` supplies placeholder values for the env vars modules validate at load. It covers the `gh` and `git` allowlists (`tests/github/gh-cli.test.ts`, `tests/github/git-cli.test.ts`), the authorization matrix with one row per kind of command and one column per caller class (`tests/github/approval.test.ts`), credential leases and token scopes (`tests/github/lease.test.ts`), the tool factories, the GitHub dispatch hooks, the memory slots on eve's in-memory file-memory backend (`tests/memory/`), decision-model triage and its `gh` helpers (`tests/triage/`), the intake contract and route handlers (`tests/intake/`), and the assembled surface as eve discovers it (`tests/surface/`).
- **Discovery diagnostics:** `pnpm run discovery` runs `eve info --json` through `scripts/discovery.ts` and fails unless the status is `ready` with 0 errors and 0 warnings. `npx eve info` prints the same report for reading, but exits 0 even when compilation fails, so it cannot gate anything by itself.
- **Evals:** `pnpm eval --tag fast` for the cheap loop; `pnpm eval pipeline/full-pipeline` deliberately runs the whole line and pushes a real branch (scratch repo recommended). Evals need model credentials and cost real tokens; `pnpm validate` only lints and type-checks them.
- `pnpm validate` bundles check + typecheck + test + discovery.

## Future considerations

- **Continuous operation:** a sweep schedule (handler mode, one dispatched session per queued item) needs cross-run dedupe state, which needs an external store; the approval policies already recognize schedule turns via `isScheduleAppAuth`.
- **Merge behind approval:** add `pr merge` to `COMMANDS` with the `ship` effect for comment-driven merges. It also needs a token scope with contents write for that one command, since `repo-triage` cannot merge.
- **Close the residual windows:** run the session clone and `FACTORY_SETUP_COMMAND` under a lease (or run the setup command after the policy is reset), pin the `gh` version in `installFactoryTooling`, and confirm token narrowing against a live installation so strict scopes can become the default.
- **More intake:** `onCheckRun`/`onWorkflowRun` (finer-grained CI intake), Sentry via an MCP connection on the analyst, Slack via eve's Slack channel. Systems that can POST JSON can already use the intake API.
- **Per-caller tool surfaces:** today the caller class changes approval outcomes, not which tools are mounted, with one exception: unattended runs are not given the brain's write tools. The same pattern could trim other tools for untrusted sessions.
- **Parallel tracks:** for large items, the analyst could split independent tracks and the orchestrator could fan out several implementer calls in one response (eve runs the batch concurrently), with non-overlapping write scopes.

## Glossary

- **eve:** the agent framework powering this app; discovers capabilities from `agent/`.
- **Channel:** an inbound/outbound surface. Here: GitHub, Linear, the intake API (a custom channel), plus the eve route's auth config.
- **Connection:** an external MCP/OpenAPI server exposed to the model. Here: `linear`.
- **Tool:** a typed action authored with `defineTool`, run in the app runtime. The `gh` and `git` tools run their commands in the mounting agent's sandbox.
- **Skill:** a load-on-demand Markdown procedure; the packaged form requires `description` frontmatter used for routing.
- **Subagent / station:** a declared agent under `agent/subagents/<id>/` with `tool: false`, so the model calls it only through its `run_<id>` workflow-tool wrapper in `agent/tools/`. It runs in a fresh child session and inherits nothing from the root (no instructions, tools, connections, memory, or sandbox), so the caller passes everything in `message`. The wrapper attaches an `outputSchema` per call via `ctx.agent(id).send(message, { outputSchema })`, blocking on `.result()` until the station answers with structured output.
- **Workflow tool:** a static tool (`defineWorkflowTool`) whose executor runs as a durable Workflow, giving it `ctx.agent()` to delegate to a subagent with a per-call `outputSchema`. Each station's `run_<id>` wrapper is one.
- **Decision model:** a model that answers closed questions (pick one, yes or no) about a shared state in one call, through eve's `decide`. Here `typesafe-ai/jev`, used for triage, label selection, duplicate checks, and CI failure diagnosis.
- **Lane:** what triage says happens next to a work item: `pipeline`, `clarify`, `answer`, or `duplicate`.
- **Memory slot:** a `defineMemory` file under an agent's `memory/` directory. eve recalls the slot's document before each turn and gives the model `<slot>__save_memory` and `<slot>__remove_memory` tools. Here: `preferences` (per user) and `brain` (per repository).
- **Factory brain:** the `brain` slot: durable, verified facts about the target repository that every run on it recalls.
- **Effect:** what a `gh` invocation does as far as authorization is concerned (`read`, `label`, `comment`, `state`, `draft-pr`, `write`, `ship`, or `forbidden`), derived from its argv by `parseGh`.
- **Credential lease:** one command's access to GitHub: a placeholder in the process, the real token swapped in at the sandbox firewall, and the policy reset when the command returns.
- **Token scope:** the permission set a leased token is requested with: `repo-read`, `repo-triage`, or `repo-push`.
- **Autonomous principal:** the constructed identity (`github:foreman-factory`) unattended runs execute under. Label-intake and CI-fix runs carry the intake issue or pull request number as an auth attribute; intake API runs carry the ticket id and the verified caller instead, and no thread. Approval policies deny it everything except labels, comments on its one stamped thread, closing or reopening issues, and draft PRs.
- **Ticket:** a work item submitted to the intake API. Its id is the address of the session that works it.
- **Vercel Connect:** brokers OAuth/credentials for GitHub and Linear; connectors are identified by a UID.
- **OIDC:** the project's Vercel identity token, used to authenticate Blob (and AI Gateway) without static keys, and accepted as a caller credential by the intake API.
